purpose: Seeds the principles and exemplar strata of the design-taste model from external award canon rather than the corpus, so the taste layer is calibrated to recognized excellence. Principles are stored knowledge; exemplars are referenced, not image-ingested, due to copyright.
weighting_note: SEGD supplies the high-design ceiling (systems, placemaking, typography). Trade contests (Signs of the Times, ISA-adjacent, regional sign associations) supply taste applied to the commercial categories Substrate shops actually quote. Exemplars are weighted toward corpus-relevant categories.

canon_sources.name: SEGD Global Design Awards
canon_sources.teaches: placemaking, wayfinding systems, typography, material innovation, connection to context

canon_sources.name: Signs of the Times Annual Sign Contest
canon_sources.teaches: shop-fabricated illuminated and non-illuminated commercial signs, channel letters, pylons, monuments, themed work

canon_sources.name: Sign trade and regional association design awards (ISA-adjacent, MSSA, etc.)
canon_sources.teaches: category criteria by sign type and size, finish and fabrication quality benchmarks

judging_criteria_consensus: Finish quality, precision, and fabrication technique
Innovation: offers something new vs. existing solutions
Aesthetics: form, color, texture, finishing, materials
Functionality and legibility in real use

principles.principle: Legibility before everything. The core message must read at the intended distance and approach speed before any styling is judged.
principles.rationale: A sign that looks beautiful in a portfolio but fails at 40mph has failed its job. Trade and design juries both score message effectiveness.

principles.principle: One primary read. Establish a single clear hierarchy: one element wins, everything else is subordinate.
principles.rationale: Competing focal points flatten the message and read as amateur.

principles.principle: Contrast must hold in every condition the sign lives in, day and night, lit and unlit.
principles.rationale: Self-storage monuments and pylons are encountered in full sun and full dark; both states must be deliberate.

principles.principle: Finish discipline. Clean returns, consistent reveals, concealed fasteners, no visible seams or light leaks.
principles.rationale: Sign juries weight finish quality and precision heavily; this is the single clearest pro-vs-amateur tell.

principles.principle: Optical correction over mechanical correctness. Overshoot rounded forms, compensate baselines and spacing for how the eye reads, not how the ruler measures.
principles.rationale: Mechanically equal looks visually uneven; corrected work reads as intentional and refined.

principles.principle: Let the fabrication method be the aesthetic. Push-thru depth, halo glow, and reveal shadows are features to design around, not hide.
principles.rationale: The strongest commercial signs use their construction as the visual idea rather than decorating over it.

principles.principle: Material honesty. Use each material for what it does well; avoid faking one material with another unless the fake is itself the craft.
principles.rationale: Juries reward suitable, durable material use; mismatches read cheap and age badly.

principles.principle: Earned color. Limit the palette; reserve accent color for the single thing that must be emphasized.
principles.rationale: Restraint makes the accent work; everything-is-loud reads as noise.

principles.principle: Negative space is a design element, not leftover. Give primary copy room to breathe.
principles.rationale: Crowded layouts lose hierarchy and legibility; space signals confidence.

principles.principle: Type restraint. Few families, deliberate weights, generous and even spacing.
principles.rationale: Type discipline is a core legibility and refinement signal across all judging frameworks.

principles.principle: Site fit. The sign should belong to its architecture and surroundings, reading as part of the place rather than applied to it.
principles.rationale: This is SEGD's central ethos: connecting people to place. It elevates even simple commercial signs.

principles.principle: Design for the actual approach. Account for viewing angle, speed, sightline obstructions, and where the viewer is when the sign matters.
principles.rationale: Wayfinding and roadside ID succeed or fail on real-world encounter, not elevation-view symmetry.

principles.principle: Dual life. Design the lit night state and the unlit day state as two intentional looks, not one with the lights off.
principles.rationale: Illuminated signs are seen in both; strong work makes each deliberate.

principles.principle: Family consistency. Across a multi-sign package, hold a consistent system of materials, type, color, and detailing.
principles.rationale: A coherent sign family reads as designed; inconsistency reads as assembled. Directly relevant to multi-sign permit and wayfinding packages.

principles.principle: Information sequencing. In wayfinding, deliver the right information at each decision point, no more, no less.
principles.rationale: Over-loading or under-serving decision points is the most common wayfinding failure.

principles.principle: Distinctiveness without gimmick. Be memorable through a strong, coherent idea, not bolted-on novelty.
principles.rationale: Innovation is an award differentiator, but juries separate genuine concept from gimmick that ages poorly.
